question: Who was the first speaker of the Indian Parliament?
solution:
The correct answer is __**GV Mavlankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar (GV Mavalankar) -

 
 
• He was the first Lok Sabha Speaker of the Indian Lok Sabha.
 
• Lok Sabha is the lower house of the Indian Parliament.
 
• He was affectionately called 'Dadasaheb'.
 
• He actively participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement and Salt Satyagraha.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Dr Rajendra Prasad:__ 

 
 
• Rajendra Prasad, (born December 3, 1884, Zeradei, India—died February 28, 1963, Patna).
 
• He was an Indian politician, lawyer, and journalist who was the first president of the Republic of India (1950–62).
 
• He also was a comrade of Mahatma Gandhi early in the noncooperation movement for independence and was president of the Indian National Congress (1934, 1939, and 1947).
 
• He gave up his law practice in 1920 to join the noncooperation movement.
 
• Becoming an active journalist in the nationalist interest, he wrote for Searchlight in English and founded and edited the Hindi weekly Desh.
 
 
 
• Dr B. R. Ambedkar (14 April 1891 - 6 December 1956):
 
 
• He was a well known political leader, philosopher, writer, economist and scholar.
 
• He was also a social reformer who dedicated his life to eradicating untouchability and social inequality in India.
 
• Chairman of the Drafting Committee which prepared the Constitution of India.
 
• Set up the 'Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha (Outcastes Welfare Association)' which was devoted to spreading education and culture amongst the untouchables.
 
• Leader of the Dalit rights movement and Dalit Buddhist movement.
 
• Books: Annihilation of Caste, The Buddha and His Dhamma, Pakistan or Partition of India, Who Were the Shudras? 
 
• Award: Bharat Ratna (posthumously in 1990)
 
• Resting place: Chaitya Bhoomi, Mumbai 
 
 
 
• KM Munshi
 
 
• KM Munshi was the President of the Order of Business Committee of the Constituent Assembly.
 
• The Order of Business Committee was responsible for planning the agenda and order of business for the Constituent Assembly sessions.
 
• KM Munshi played a significant role in the drafting of the Indian Constitution and was a member of the Drafting Committee.
 
• He was an influential figure in the freedom struggle and later contributed to the shaping of independent India's governance structure.
